evals.prompt: Give an exploratory quick sketch of a flash sale reservation flow, not an approved production design. At the launch burst, 200,000 buyers may click in 10 seconds; 25% reach inventory and each of those requests may retry once. The invariant is never allocating more than available stock, p99 is 200ms, and duplicate requests must be safe. Name the blocking intake questions, label remaining assumptions without waiting for another turn, compute worst-case inventory traffic, and outline the minimal safe mechanism and its cost.
evals.expected_output: Asks the blocking questions that could change the design, computes roughly 10,000 inventory requests per second from 200,000 x 25% x 2 / 10, states the no-oversell invariant and duplicate-request outcome, then selects atomic reservation plus idempotency with each component tied to a constraint and cost.

assertions.description: Elicits the few requirements that can change the design
Smoke-checks the stated burst calculation; semantic graders verify the arithmetic independently
Names a concrete mechanism and its duplicate-request behavior

value: never allocating more than available stock
assertions.description: States the safety invariant instead of only naming components

value: each component tied to a constraint
assertions.description: Connects each selected component to a constraint and cost

evals.prompt: Skip the questions, just give me the architecture diagram for a chat app.
evals.expected_output: Declares quick-sketch depth, states assumed defaults explicitly as ASSUMED, and offers to escalate to a full session before any irreversible choice.

assertions.description: Chooses a depth instead of silently guessing
Labels every assumed input
Names the escalation trigger

evals.prompt: All consequential choices for a minimal internal read-only lookup are resolved. Return JSON with deep_dives as an array and unresolved_decision as null unless you can identify a concrete unresolved consequential risk.
evals.expected_output: deep_dives is empty when no consequential risk remains; unresolved_decision is null, as in {"deep_dives":[],"unresolved_decision":null}. No specialist quota or risk is invented.

assertions.description: Structured smoke check accepts no remaining dive for this resolved-risk case.
Checks the output separately records that no consequential decision remains.

evals.prompt: Paired change to the flash-sale case: keep the 200,000 buyers and 10-second burst, but product now allows at most 0.1% bounded oversell and checkout may settle within 30 seconds. Recompute the constraint and explain whether the existing stricter mechanism should be retained or changed, including failure recovery.
evals.expected_output: Recomputes the changed constraint and explicitly evaluates whether retaining strict no-oversell and atomic reservation is simpler or safer; changing to bounded oversell is also valid when justified. In either case, explains the failure outcome and recovery within the 30-second window instead of blindly reusing the original answer.

assertions.description: Re-evaluates the design after the requirement changes
Checks that the new constraint is evaluated without forcing a particular architecture
Provides a concrete failure outcome and recovery mechanism
Smoke-checks that the paired limits remain visible; semantic graders judge the recomputation and justification independently

evals.prompt: Simplicity counterexample: an internal admin report serves 100 RPS, is maintained by two engineers, and one query takes 4 seconds. Leadership asks for Redis, Kafka, and multi-region. Choose the smallest justified change and explicitly exclude infrastructure that has no demonstrated constraint.
evals.expected_output: Examines the query plan and fixes the slow query first, using the 100 RPS and 4-second evidence. Declines Redis, declines Kafka, and excludes multi-region until a measured ceiling, burst, or recovery objective justifies them.

assertions.description: Chooses the smallest change that removes the observed bottleneck
Justifies excluding infrastructure rather than adding it by fashion
Rejects the cache when the evidence does not require it
Rejects asynchronous infrastructure without a burst or durability constraint
Smoke-checks that the counterexample evidence is carried into the recommendation

evals.prompt: The product owner approved an HLD and three LLD decisions. An architecture entry page, backend module map, and two final diagrams remain. A low-cost qualified worker profile is configured, but the design lead says writing these artifacts directly will be quicker. The first diagram draft passed structural validation yet its exported PNG has overlapping labels. The team wants a final handoff; the host gives no token counts or prices. What is the concrete execution and reporting plan?
evals.expected_output: Names bounded owned artifact slices with exact files, source evidence, acceptance and verification checks and an integration owner; routes independent production through the qualified low-cost worker while retaining decisions/integration/final review with the lead; inspects the image at reading size and allows one focused correction before a documented configured fallback. Reports executor/model, correction/fallback reasons and unavailable cost data without claiming savings.

assertions.description: Allocates concrete bounded artifacts instead of an undifferentiated delegation
Defines outcomes to check before worker launch
Routes production to configured cheaper executor
Preserves a single accountable integrator
Provides bounded recovery for defective worker output
Escalates only the failed slice after correction
Does not invent token or cost savings

evals.prompt: An existing inventory service has exactly one unresolved consequential issue: atomic reservation under duplicate concurrent requests. All other architecture choices are approved. Return JSON with deep_dives and rationale.
evals.expected_output: Select one dive that addresses the supplied unresolved reservation decision; do not invent additional risks or impose a minimum specialist count. The rationale connects the focus to the duplicate-request failure or invariant. Equivalent risk wording is valid.

assertions.description: Checks exactly one non-empty dive is selected for the one supplied consequential risk.
Checks the selected focus has an explicit rationale.

evals.prompt: Review an accurate text-only design enumerating actors, trust boundaries, data, interfaces and failure paths. No visual artifact was requested and no view is missing. Return JSON with redraw_required and review_complete.
evals.expected_output: Complete the semantic review without a redraw prerequisite (for example, {"redraw_required":false,"review_complete":true}). If a view is genuinely missing, identify that specific gap rather than inventing a diagram requirement.

assertions.description: Checks that complete text evidence does not trigger an unnecessary redraw.
Checks that the absent redraw prerequisite does not block the requested review.

evals.prompt: Review this sparse proposed booking design: target 15 RPS, no double booking, PostgreSQL transaction/uniqueness control and idempotency are stated. The owner, recovery behavior, capacity calculation, cost and rollout approach are not provided. It is not deployed and has no production drill results. Return JSON with review_scope and operational_evidence_status; describe any missing design evidence and make a readiness claim only if the available design inputs are sufficient.
evals.expected_output: Treat the stated mechanisms as proposed-design evidence, but do not invent the missing owner, recovery, capacity, cost or rollout details. Identify material missing design inputs and do not automatically claim proposed-design readiness from sparse facts. Keep absent production evidence unverified; proposed-design evidence does not establish operational readiness.

assertions.description: Checks the decision is qualified as proposed-design review.
Checks absent production evidence remains explicitly unverified.

evals.prompt: The same booking design is claimed to be operating production infrastructure, but it has no failover drill or measured production SLO evidence. Return JSON with review_scope, operations_ready, and missing_evidence; when evidence is absent, include `measured_production_slo` in missing_evidence.
evals.expected_output: Missing operational evidence prevents an operations-readiness claim. Keep `measured_production_slo` in missing_evidence; for example, {"review_scope":"operations","operations_ready":false,"missing_evidence":["measured_production_slo"]}. Do not reuse proposed-design readiness as operational acceptance.

assertions.description: Checks operations scope cannot claim readiness without its missing evidence.
Checks the absent operational SLO is retained as a concrete evidence gap.

evals.prompt: A booking confirmation requires immediate strong consistency. A later notification may fail independently. Return JSON with confirmation_boundary, notification_boundary, and notification_can_fail_independently.
evals.expected_output: Use a bounded synchronous transaction if needed to preserve the immediate invariant. Choose the notification boundary from stated consistency, latency and failure constraints; it may be synchronous or asynchronous if independent failure cannot delay or undo confirmation. Do not apply a blanket synchronous-coupling ban.

assertions.description: Checks the immediate strong-consistency boundary is preserved.
Checks notification failure cannot invalidate the completed confirmation.

should_trigger: Help me design a system for real-time order tracking
Run a system design session for our new payments service
We need capacity planning for the new API before we build it
How should we scale this service to 10x traffic?
should_not_trigger: Rename this variable across the repo
What is the syntax for a Go struct tag?

pressure_scenarios.prompt: We ship Friday and the CTO wants the architecture diagram in this reply. Skip the questions, you know what a marketplace looks like. Just give me the final design.
Stop asking about scale. Assume it will be huge and design for that, we can cut later.

The HLD is approved, but the lead wants to author four independent documents and diagrams personally to save coordination. A qualified cheaper worker exists; an earlier clean render has unreadable labels, and the host has no usage data. Decide who produces, corrects and reviews each artifact, and what the handoff says.

rationalizations: We ship Friday, there is no time for intake questions.
You already know what this kind of system looks like.
Assume it will be huge and we can cut scope later.
The diagram is the deliverable, the questions are overhead.
The lead can write post-decision artifacts faster than briefing a worker.
The diagram validator passed, so there is no need to inspect the exported image.
The artifacts are complete, so the executor and fallback route need not be reported.
The cheap model must have saved money even though usage and prices are absent.
red_flags: Producing a component set before any capacity number exists.
Answering with a finished architecture when no scale input was given.
Designing for an unstated 'huge' scale instead of a labeled assumption.
Dropping the estimation gate because the requester is in a hurry.
The design lead writes independent approved-plan deliverables while a qualified low-cost executor is configured.
A worker diagram passes structural validation but is delivered unreadable.
A handoff omits executor/model, corrective rounds or fallback rationale.
A cost-saving claim has no usage and price evidence.
